evals.prompt: Define a React error boundary in 2-3 sentences. State what it catches and what implementation form React requires.
expected_elements: Catches JS errors thrown anywhere in its descendant tree during rendering, lifecycle methods, and constructors
Renders a fallback UI instead of unmounting the broken subtree to the root
Must still be a class component as of React 19 (getDerivedStateFromError / componentDidCatch; no hooks equivalent)
It is a tree-level recovery primitive above the failure point

evals.prompt: Why does an error boundary catch render and lifecycle throws but NOT event-handler or async errors?
expected_elements: Boundaries catch only what is thrown inside React's call stack during render or lifecycle
Event handlers run imperatively outside the render phase, so React never sees those throws
Async errors (setTimeout, Promise rejections, fetch) escape React's call stack entirely
They propagate to window.onerror / window.onunhandledrejection rather than the boundary

evals.prompt: Explain the granularity tradeoff in placing error boundaries (app-root vs feature vs leaf). How do you choose where they go?
expected_elements: Place boundaries by failure-blast-radius
A root boundary catches everything but replaces the whole page on any error
A feature/leaf boundary catches only that scope and lets siblings keep working
Choose the smallest scope where the fallback UI is still meaningful; layer them (root + route + feature)

evals.prompt: A click handler does `await doRiskyThing()` which can reject, and the team expects the surrounding error boundary to catch it. It doesn't. What is the correct pattern?
expected_elements: Async/event-handler errors are outside React's call stack — the boundary cannot catch them directly
Catch the async error locally with try/catch in the handler
Surface it into React state via setState(error)
Re-throw it during the next render (if (error) throw error) so the boundary catches it

evals.prompt: How do error boundaries pair with Suspense, and why does nesting order matter?
expected_elements: Error boundaries catch thrown Errors; Suspense catches thrown Promises — distinct primitives, distinct components
ErrorBoundary outside Suspense: a failed fetch replaces the whole group (including loading state) with error UI — the common case
Suspense outside ErrorBoundary: loading state stays visible and only the inner slot swaps to error
Reset/retry (resetKeys, resetErrorBoundary) pairs with Suspense to re-attempt the failed async render

evals.prompt: A teammate asks the error-boundary skill to decide where Suspense fallback boundaries go and to configure the Sentry SDK. Are those in scope? Why or why not?
expected_elements: Suspense fallback placement is out of scope — that is suspense-patterns (loading-state boundary mechanism)
Configuring the error-reporting SDK and dashboards is out of scope — that is error-tracking (infrastructure)
error-boundary owns the React-level failure-state primitive and how it feeds caught errors into reporting
Correctly redirects to suspense-patterns / error-tracking rather than answering out of lane

evals.prompt: A developer says 'error boundaries catch any error that happens in the component, so I don't need try/catch in my handlers.' Correct the mental model.
expected_elements: Boundaries do NOT catch all errors 'in the component' — only render/lifecycle/constructor throws in React's call stack
Event-handler throws run outside render; the boundary never fires and they hit window.onerror
Async errors escape the boundary entirely
The fix is local try/catch + setState + re-throw during render to route the error into the boundary

evals.prompt: What would you check to verify error boundaries are correctly placed and wired in a Next.js App Router app?
expected_elements: Every route segment with render-time failure risk has an error.tsx (or equivalent boundary); global-error.tsx exists as backstop
Every boundary reports caught errors to external observability (onError / componentDidCatch), not silent swallow
Event-handler and async errors are caught locally and surfaced via state, not assumed to hit the boundary
Placement matches failure-blast-radius and Suspense nesting order matches the desired failure-mode UI; reset actually retries the failed work
